Format an integer number of cents as a US dollar amount with exactly two fractional digits and comma thousands separators. Place a negative sign before the dollar sign for negative values. Zero and positive values have no sign.
reference_solution:
def format_cents(cents: int) -> str:
    sign = "-" if cents < 0 else ""
    dollars, remainder = divmod(abs(cents), 100)
    return f"{sign}${dollars:,}.{remainder:02d}"

signature: def overlap_minutes(start_a: str, end_a: str, start_b: str, end_b: str) -> int
spec: Return the number of overlapping minutes between two half-open datetime intervals [start_a, end_a) and [start_b, end_b). Inputs are ISO-format naive datetime strings, and each end is not earlier than its corresponding start. Intervals that only touch at an endpoint have zero overlap.
reference_solution:
from datetime import datetime

def overlap_minutes(start_a: str, end_a: str, start_b: str, end_b: str) -> int:
    a_start = datetime.fromisoformat(start_a)
    a_end = datetime.fromisoformat(end_a)
    b_start = datetime.fromisoformat(start_b)
    b_end = datetime.fromisoformat(end_b)
    overlap_start = max(a_start, b_start)
    overlap_end = min(a_end, b_end)
    return max(0, int((overlap_end - overlap_start).total_seconds() // 60))

signature: def next_weekday(day: str, weekday: int) -> str

Return whether year is a leap year in the Gregorian calendar. A year divisible by 4 is a leap year unless it is divisible by 100, except that years divisible by 400 are leap years.
reference_solution:
def is_leap_year(year: int) -> bool:
    return year % 4 == 0 and (year % 100 != 0 or year % 400 == 0)

signature: def ceil_divide(numerator: int, denominator: int) -> int:
spec: Return the mathematical ceiling of numerator divided by denominator. Numerator may be negative and denominator is a positive integer. Do not return a float.
reference_solution:
def ceil_divide(numerator: int, denominator: int) -> int:
    return -(-numerator // denominator)

signature: def weighted_mean(values: list[float], weights: list[float]) -> float:

signature: def compound_balance(principal: float, annual_rate: float, years: int) -> float:
spec: Return the balance after annual compounding for years whole years. annual_rate is a percentage, so 5 means five percent per year. Round the final balance to two decimal places using decimal round-half-up semantics.

signature: def nearest_multiple_down(value: int, multiple: int) -> int:
spec: Return the greatest integer multiple of positive multiple that is less than or equal to value. This is mathematical floor behavior, including for negative values. The returned value is an integer.
reference_solution:
def nearest_multiple_down(value: int, multiple: int) -> int:
    return (value // multiple) * multiple

The domain has at least two dot-separated labels, and every label is 1 through 63 characters, begins and ends with an ASCII letter or digit, and otherwise uses only ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens.

Return True only when `text` has the exact form `YYYY-MM-DD`, where all eight date characters are ASCII digits. The year must be from 1 through 9999, and the month and day must form a real Gregorian calendar date. Return False otherwise.

Return True only when `text` is 8 through 32 characters long and every character is printable ASCII from `!` through `~`. It must contain at least one ASCII lowercase letter, one ASCII uppercase letter, one ASCII digit, and one character that is not an ASCII letter or digit. Return False otherwise.
reference_solution:
def is_valid_password(text: str) -> bool:
    if not isinstance(text, str) or not 8 <= len(text) <= 32:
        return False
    if any(not ("!" <= ch <= "~") for ch in text):
        return False
    lower = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    upper = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
    digits = "0123456789"
    return (any(ch in lower for ch in text) and
            any(ch in upper for ch in text) and
            any(ch in digits for ch in text) and
            any(ch not in lower + upper + digits for ch in text))
